sections.title: Contents
sections.summary: The 'Contents' section outlines the structure of a white paper on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). It lists three main sections: Section 1 covers RAG industrialization, landscape, and strategy; Section 2 details 'RAG Recipes' for real-world challenges like data-driven chunking and multimodal reasoning; and Section 3 provides a deep dive into RAG evaluation and metrics. The table also includes preliminary sections like 'About This White Paper' and concluding sections such as 'References', 'Authors', and 'Acknowledgements'.

sections.title: About This White Paper
sections.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/About This White Paper
sections.summary: This section outlines the background, purpose, and design principles of the white paper. It explains that the document is based on studies and roundtable discussions regarding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), aiming to analyze industry demands and facilitate strategy development. The design principles emphasize simplifying complexity and fostering intuitiveness through visual illustrations. Additionally, it details how to use the white paper by describing three main sections: RAG Industrialization Landscape & Strategy, RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges, and a Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.summary: The 'Key Takeaways' section summarizes the white paper's three main parts. It highlights that RAG solutions are essential for sustainable industrial knowledge retrieval due to their trustworthiness and cost efficiency, though resource constraints must be managed. It introduces five recipes for real-world challenges like limited data and complex contexts, emphasizing improved retrieval quality through strategies like metadata filtering and hybrid search. Finally, it notes the complexity of RAG evaluation involving multiple metrics and the industry's need for a standardized framework to ensure consistent quality and scalability.

sections.title: Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy
sections.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy

children.title: Let's Start with a Crash Course of RAG
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy/Let's Start with a Crash Course of RAG
children.summary: This section provides an overview of the challenges associated with using Large Language Models (LLMs) in isolation, such as hallucinations, knowledge cutoffs, and lack of access to private data. It illustrates these issues with examples involving historical figures like Igor Stravinsky and Béla Bartók. The content then details the importance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for enterprises by listing key benefits including trustworthiness, consistency, controllability, auditability, process optimization, IP security, cost efficiency, scalability, and multi-step reasoning capabilities.

children.title: Wait! Naive RAG Doesn't Work Well!
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy/Wait! Naive RAG Doesn't Work Well!
children.summary: This page provides a crash course on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), defining it as a method that pairs LLMs with external databases. It details the four stages of RAG: Pre-retrieval, Retrieval, Post-retrieval, and Augmentation & Generation. A central diagram illustrates this workflow using a query about a debate between Elon Musk and Yann LeCun to demonstrate how RAG retrieves relevant context to generate an answer compared to a standard LLM response. The bottom section poses an 'Interesting Question' regarding whether long context windows can solve all data retrieval issues.

children.title: So, What Are Some Techniques to Enhance RAG?
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy/So, What Are Some Techniques to Enhance RAG?
children.summary: This section introduces 12 advanced or modular RAG techniques designed to enhance different components of a RAG system. It presents a chart that plots these techniques based on their 'Degree of Complexity' (considering resource consumption, cost, latency, etc.) versus their 'Projected Contribution to Overall Quality & Trustworthiness'. The identified techniques include Metadata Filtering, Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE), Query Engineering & Fusion, Routing, Search Module & Hybrid Search, Task Adapter, Adaptive Retrieval & Self-RAG, Multiple Indexing Structures, Information or Context Compression, Extra Generation & Predicting, Memory, and Retrieval-augmented Reasoning (RAT & RAGAR).

children.title: And What Tools Can I Use to Develop a RAG System?
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy/And What Tools Can I Use to Develop a RAG System?
children.summary: This page, titled 'So, What Are Some Techniques to Enhance RAG?', outlines twelve distinct strategies for improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. The techniques are presented in a grid format and include Metadata Filtering, Query Engineering & Fusion, Task Adapter, Memory, Information or Context Compression, Extra Generation & Predicting, Routing, Multiple Indexing Structures, Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE), Search Module & Hybrid Search, Adaptive Retrieval & Self-RAG, and Retrieval-augmented Reasoning (RAT & RAGAR). Each section details the main improvement areas (such as Retrieval, Augmentation, or Generation) and explains the specific methods used.

children.title: Alright, How Can I Strategically Prioritize My Development Focus to Industrialize a RAG Project?
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 1: RAG Industrialization - Landscape & Strategy/Alright, How Can I Strategically Prioritize My Development Focus to Industrialize a RAG Project?
children.summary: This section outlines the strategic framework for industrializing a RAG project, structured as 'The RAG Industrialization Journey'. It details four key dimensions—Core Development Focus, Key Challenges, Key Capabilities, and Key Metrics—across five distinct phases: Ideation, Prototyping, Proof of Concept (PoC), Best-known Methods (BKM), and Operation. The content provides specific tasks, potential obstacles, required skills, and performance indicators relevant to each phase of the development lifecycle.

sections.title: Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges
sections.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges

children.title: The Cold Start Recipe: Data-Driven Chunking & Embedding Strategy Without Evaluation Dataset
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The Cold Start Recipe: Data-Driven Chunking & Embedding Strategy Without Evaluation Dataset
children.summary: This section outlines a 'Cold Start Recipe' for establishing data-driven chunking and embedding strategies in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems when an evaluation dataset is unavailable. It addresses challenges such as the scarcity of expert-constructed datasets and resource constraints. The core methodology involves analyzing pairwise cosine similarity scores to assess embedding quality, drawing on research by Nguyen et al. that compares general LLMs (GPT-3) with domain-specific models (AstroLLaMA). A higher variance in similarity scores indicates better semantic representation. The section concludes with a practical application of this analytics approach to the 'appliedAI AI Act White Paper', utilizing Langchain tools like CharacterTextSplitter and QAGenerationChain to generate synthetic question-answer pairs for initial system assessment.

children.title: The Virtual Havruta Recipe: Optimizing Queries for Multifaceted Contexts & Precise Citations
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The Virtual Havruta Recipe: Optimizing Queries for Multifaceted Contexts & Precise Citations
children.summary: This page details the results of a 'Cold Start Recipe' for data-driven chunking and embedding strategies. It compares two models, text-embedding-ada-002 and albert-small-v2, using tables to show pairwise cosine similarity distributions, RAGAS metrics (like Context Precision and Answer Relevance), and specific QA examples. The bottom section introduces a prototype RAG Cold Start Analytic App developed by appliedAI Initiative, which features grid search experiments, automatic evaluation, and exploratory data analysis visualizations.

children.title: The Deepset Recipe: Unlocking the Mastery of Metadata for Filtering, Searching, and Reranking
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The Deepset Recipe: Unlocking the Mastery of Metadata for Filtering, Searching, and Reranking
children.summary: This document page outlines the 'Virtual Havruta Recipe,' a project designed to optimize queries for multifaceted contexts and precise citations in Jewish scripture study. It details the background, goals, and challenges addressed by this RAG-based system, such as incomplete queries and non-aligned reranking. The page further explains the query engineering process, including screening, editing, and adapting user inputs into primary and secondary source queries, alongside metadata filtering strategies.

children.title: The Jina AI Recipe: Agent-Driven SQL Scoping and Task-Specific Finetuning for Patent Search
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The Jina AI Recipe: Agent-Driven SQL Scoping and Task-Specific Finetuning for Patent Search
children.summary: This section outlines 'The Jina AI Recipe' for patent search, which utilizes agent-driven SQL scoping and task-specific finetuning. It addresses challenges like inadequate precision in classic search methods by implementing LLM agents to construct dynamic SQL queries for filtering. The process involves establishing a baseline, implementing out-of-the-box improvements, and applying task-specific finetuning (e.g., LoRA) to optimize embedding models for domain-specific texts, ultimately improving retrieval quality.

children.title: The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking

children.title: Background & Goals of this Recipe
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/Background & Goals of this Recipe
children.summary: This section outlines the background and goals of the RAGAR recipe, which addresses the increasing prevalence of misinformation in political discourse. It introduces RAG-augmented reasoning (RAGAR) approaches, specifically Chain of RAG (CoRAG) and Tree of RAG (ToRAG), combined with Chain of Verification for evidence-based fact-checking. The text notes that while originally designed for political fact-checking, the method is repurposable for various industry applications requiring thorough verification.

children.title: Challenges Addressed
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/Challenges Addressed
children.summary: The section titled 'Challenges Addressed' outlines three primary difficulties in multimodal fact-checking. These include Contextualized Multimodal Claim Generation, which involves generating claims from text while filtering relevant image details; Open-ended Multimodal Evidence Retrieval, focusing on retrieving text and image evidence with correct timeframes and source filtering; and Dynamic, Agentic Reasoning Actions, which requires managing prompts to determine logical reasoning paths and when to stop based on evidence accumulation.

children.title: The RAGAR Approaches: Chain of RAG (CoRAG) & Tree of RAG (ToRAG)
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/The RAGAR Approaches: Chain of RAG (CoRAG) & Tree of RAG (ToRAG)
children.summary: This section illustrates the RAGAR approaches, specifically comparing Chain of RAG (CoRAG) and Tree of RAG (ToRAG). It details a workflow starting with a 'Claim' and 'Multimodal Claim Generation' to produce context. The CoRAG approach is depicted as a linear sequence where questions are generated one by one, each followed by a RAG process to create QA pairs. In contrast, the ToRAG approach shows a branching structure where multiple questions are generated in parallel, processed through RAG, and then undergo 'QA Elimination' steps to filter results before proceeding to the next level. Both methods ultimately collect QA pairs for 'Veracity Prediction', resulting in a label and explanation.

children.title: The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking

children.title: RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Chain of RAG)
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Chain of RAG)
children.summary: The section titled 'RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Chain of RAG)' outlines a linear workflow for fact-checking using multimodal data. It begins with a specific claim and image context regarding Mike Pompeo. The process involves a decision loop where the system determines if an image question is needed; if yes, it uses Google Reverse Image Search API to find relevant evidence, otherwise it performs standard Evidence Retrieval via DuckDuckGo Search. A follow-up check determines if further questioning is required before generating a final Veracity Label and Explanation.

children.title: RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Tree of RAG)
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Tree of RAG)
children.summary: This section details the 'RAG-Augmented Reasoning Technique (Tree of RAG)', a multimodal fact-checking workflow. It begins with a specific claim and image context, then branches into parallel processing paths ('Question/Followup Branch'). Each path independently evaluates an image using either Google Reverse Image Search or DuckDuckGo Evidence Retrieval to generate multiple QA pairs. These pairs undergo elimination before a final decision on whether follow-up is required, ultimately leading to a veracity label.

children.title: Chain of RAG & Tree of RAG
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/Chain of RAG & Tree of RAG
children.summary: This section outlines two methodologies for RAG-augmented reasoning: Chain of RAG (CoRAG) and Tree of RAG (ToRAG). CoRAG utilizes sequential follow-up questions to retrieve further evidence and includes an early termination check to determine if sufficient information has been gathered. ToRAG creates question branches at each step of the reasoning process, eliminating pairs until only the best branch is chosen based on relevance, detail, additional information, and answer confidence.

children.title: RAG-enhanced Agents for Enterprises
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 2: RAG Recipes for Real-World Challenges/The RAGAR Recipe: Multimodal RAG-augmented Reasoning for Fact-checking/RAG-enhanced Agents for Enterprises
children.summary: This section discusses the transformative potential of RAG-enhanced agents in enterprise solutions. It highlights how the combination of Generative AI, advanced information retrieval, and Large Language Models (LLMs) enables intelligent agents to handle complex applications such as decision-making and strategic planning.

children.title: Now, how do we assess RAG systems?
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 3: A Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics/Now, how do we assess RAG systems?
children.summary: The page is a section header titled 'Section 3: A Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics'. It introduces the third part of a document, which focuses on evaluating and measuring performance metrics for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.

children.title: A Further Look into Existing RAG Evaluation Frameworks
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 3: A Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics/A Further Look into Existing RAG Evaluation Frameworks
children.summary: The section titled 'A Further Look into Existing RAG Evaluation Frameworks' presents a comprehensive comparison table of various frameworks used for evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. The table details the features, capabilities, and metrics supported by each framework, including Giskard, promptfoo, Ragas, DeepEval, agenta, Trulens, Tonic Validate, LangChain, LangSmith, LlamaIndex, Haystack, Deepset Cloud, and UpTrain.

children.title: Unveiling the Mechanisms Behind These Metrics
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 3: A Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics/Unveiling the Mechanisms Behind These Metrics
children.summary: This page presents a comprehensive table titled 'An Intuitive View of Key RAG Metrics in Common Practice,' which details various evaluation metrics for Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. The table lists 12 specific metrics, including Context Relevance, Precision@k, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MMR), and Answer Correctness. For each metric, it provides a description of what is measured, an intuitive formula representation, and a plain-language explanation of the calculation.

children.title: Reflections and Future Opportunities in RAG Technology
children.path: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Realized.pdf/Section 3: A Deep Dive into RAG Evaluation & Metrics/Reflections and Future Opportunities in RAG Technology
children.summary: This document page, titled 'Reflections and Future Opportunities in RAG Technology', outlines key strategic insights regarding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The top section details three main areas: industrialization landscape and strategy, recipes for real-world challenges like data scarcity, and a deep dive into evaluation metrics. The bottom section, 'Future Opportunities in RAG Technology', highlights six potential advancements including seamless integration with other systems, reasoning agents, standardized evaluation frameworks, coordinated modules, cross-modal capabilities, and sustainability.

sections.title: References
sections.summary: This page features a quote discussing how Generative AI and RAG capabilities revolutionize knowledge management by enabling employees to retrieve internal information as effectively as asking a human. The quote is attributed to Bernhard Pflugfelder, Head of Innovation Lab (GenAI) for the applied AI initiative. The footer indicates this content is from 'RAG: Strategic & Technical Insights' on page 31.
